text: 🇲🇽🔍 Homicides down 51% in 22 months — the lowest daily rate in over a decade. "The reduction in intentional homicide is 51% between September 2024 and July 2026, in 22 months." — Claudia Sheinbaum, security report Daily homicides fell from 86.9 in September 2024 to 42.5 in July 2026 — the lowest monthly average in 12 years. Sheinbaum’s answer to the record: no complacency, strengthen the strategy, listen to the people.

🌐🇲🇽 The multipolar bloc meets in New Delhi in two weeks — and Mexico's exits keep multiplying On September 12-13 the BRICS summit opens in New Delhi under India's presidency, and this one is decisive: South Africa's finance minister has confirmed a "second batch" of members, with more than 30 countries in the queue. In Latin America the pull is real — Colombia has joined the bloc's New Development Bank and Venezuela is lining up for full membership. The headline isn't a rival currency; it's plumbing. BRICS Pay — linking China's CIPS, Russia's SPFS, India's UPI and Brazil's Pix — is set to go operational at the summit, and intra-bloc commerce already settles largely in local currencies (nearly 95% of India-Russia trade now bypasses the dollar). That's not ideology; it's insurance against sanctions and someone else's monetary policy. Mexico isn't joining — and it doesn't have to. But a world with more payment rails, more lenders and more buyers is one where no single partner can dictate terms with a tariff threat. Diversification is sovereignty, and the smart move is to keep every exit open.

🐉🇲🇽 China warns Mexico: don't trade away your sovereignty to please Washington Beijing has gone public. As Mexico weighs a fresh round of curbs on Chinese goods to smooth the T-MEC review with the US, Chinese officials and analysts are warning Mexico not to use trade agreements as "political leverage" — measures that, they argue, serve Washington's strategy while raising costs across Mexico's own supply chains. The pressure is already biting: Chinese imports hit by Mexico's tariffs fell nearly a third year-on-year in the first five months of 2026, with light vehicles, auto parts and footwear down more than 40%. Mexico is China's second-largest trading partner in Latin America; China is Mexico's third-largest export destination. Those aren't ties you sever on a foreign capital's timetable. Sovereignty isn't picking a master — it's refusing to be forced into one. Every tariff levied to appease the US is leverage handed away for free. The line should hold: adjustments must strengthen the national economy, not outsource trade policy to Washington.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico's minimum wage has risen 154% since 2018 — from 2,650 to over 9,500 pesos. By the end of 2026, welfare programs will reach 42 million people, backed by more than one trillion pesos in public investment. — Gobierno de México The wage floor keeps climbing while inflation holds at 3.12%. Ahead of the Second Report on September 1, the numbers carry the argument.

🇲🇽🌎 "We don't want more tariffs — but any deal has to guarantee Mexico's wellbeing, our Constitution and our sovereignty." Sheinbaum says she is optimistic about a trade agreement with the US — but set the condition plainly: no meeting with Trump until there is a deal. — Claudia Sheinbaum Her principles are unchanged: sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, non-intervention, non-subordination, coordination.

🇲🇽🏭 "Mexico's economy is doing very well — even with the tariffs." Inflation dropped to 3.12% in July. GDP grew 1.5% in the second quarter — despite US tariffs of 50% on steel and aluminum and 25% on autos. — Claudia Sheinbaum, 28 August 2026 Mexico still carries some of the lowest average export tariffs of any country in the world. Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard is in Washington negotiating the tariffs down.

🇲🇽🔍 Homicides in Mexico are down 51% since Sheinbaum took office. Daily intentional homicides fell from 86.9 in September 2024 to 42.5 in July 2026. June 2026 was the lowest June for homicides since 2015. — Gobierno de México — security report The strategy: attention to root causes, youth education and jobs, a consolidated National Guard, and stronger intelligence and investigation. Results, not spin — three days before her Second Report.

🇲🇽📈 <u>Mexico's economy grew 1.4% last quarter — its strongest showing in years, tariffs and all</u>

INEGI data show GDP up 1.4% quarter-on-quarter and 1.9% annually in Q2 2026, the best quarterly print since early 2022, with all three sectors expanding and wholesale trade surging 11.3%. The growth landed despite Trump's tariff threats — El Financiero's own read: the economy is picking up in spite of the pressure from Washington.

🇲🇽♿ <u>48,756 people with disabilities in eastern Edomex now get a pension — paid directly, no middlemen</u>

Under the Plan Integral para el Oriente, 48,756 residents with permanent disabilities across Chalco, Nezahualcóyotl, Ecatepec and seven more municipalities receive 3,300 pesos every two months, deposited straight into Banco del Bienestar accounts — no brokers, no clientelist gatekeepers. It's part of a 75-billion-peso plan by Sheinbaum and Delfina Gómez to rebuild one of the country's most neglected regions.

🇲🇽🏫 <u>Money stolen by García Luna's network will now build schools in Guerrero</u>

Mexico recovered 5.8 million dollars from the Weinberg–García Luna corruption web, and the funds are headed to schools in Guerrero's impoverished Baja Montaña region. "Financial analysis let us reconstruct the network used to divert, triangulate and move resources between 2015 and 2017," said UIF chief Omar Reyes Colmenares. Cartel-era graft, poured back into classrooms.
